# Physical side borders in vertical merges

Original six-page OOXML control generated by
`tools/merged_side_borders_fixture.py`, with the native reference PDF output.
Each page has three 36pt physical rows and a vertically merged first column.
The cases cover a restart-only border, a missing middle border, continuation-only
borders, explicit nil/none against an inherited table border, and an opposing
neighbor border. No template artwork or third-party engine is included.

The reference application paints each physical row's side independently. A missing continuation side
does not repeat the restart border. A neighboring inherited or direct border
can still win the ordinary conflict resolution; nil is not an instruction to
erase the neighboring cell's ink.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.66 (tcBorders) and 17.4.84 (vMerge) specify cell
borders and merge membership. The reference application's per-physical-row side ownership is recorded
explicitly here; merging content does not homogenize the edge declarations.
The existing row-exception segmentation/pagination path now applies to all
vertical merges. Horizontal border ownership and row geometry are unchanged.

The native recorder samples the interior of each colored border and binds the
reference to source/PDF SHA-256 hashes. It retains PDFium bitmap ownership until
the pixels are copied. Unit tests compare presence and color; browser tests
compare native pixels through no-edit export, insertion, exact undo and reopen.
Existing row-exception/page-cut tests cover clipping of physical segments.
